rationale: Every artifact use of claim C-EVID-003 consistently preserves its scope and limitations. The claim states that rare-event simulation 'can estimate a risk metric conditional on a modeled traffic distribution, simulator and safety threshold, rather than proving unconditional safety from total test miles,' and explicitly notes it is 'not a regulatory method.' The supplied evidence (S-EVID-003-R1, S-EVID-003-R2) supports this conditional nature. All artifacts (assurance_case.json, amlas_maa_easa_crosswalk.md, research/contributions/assurance_evidence/findings.md, video/script.md, video/nextgen_structure/narration_evidence_map.md, video/nextgen_structure/script_outline.md, video/nextgen_structure/treatment.md, video/nextgen_structure/visual_inventory.md, resource_composition/whitepaper.md) either directly quote the conditional nature, explicitly state the dependencies (simulator fidelity, distribution tails, threshold), or mandate qualifiers like 'conditional estimate' and 'never proves probability of safety.' They also reinforce that the method is not a universal safety metric or a regulatory approval, aligning with the claim's stated scope and the challenge's emphasis on independent validation of assumptions.
